newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 28.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 28.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australia's fifth largest bank, St George Bank Ltd, has joined ANZ in passing on the full 0.5 percent official rate cut to mortgage customers. St George said late on Tuesday it had cut its standard variable home loan to 7.05 percent from 7.55 percent. The other major banks have so far only cut their rates to 7.2 percent from 7.55 percent.
ANZ's first half profit result is also due out later on Wednesday. Analysts expect a modest rise to between A$580 million to A$630 million.

National Mutual Holdings Ltd (NMH) on Tuesday reported a better than expected half-year profit, bolstered by strong investment returns. NMH's net earnings surged 18 percent to A$175.52 million for the six months to March 31, about A$40 million higher than analysts' average forecasts of A$134 million.

PrimeStar Partners has reached a tentative agreement for News Corp Ltd to join the satellite-dish TV service as a partner, according to a source close to the matter. The two sides are continuing their discussions, which were described as fragile and ongoing, and it was possible the deal could still unravel, the source said.

Escondida's cathodes plant has yet to fix a series of production glitches that have prevented it from reaching design capacity of 80,000 tonnes a year, company officials said. But Escondida, majority owned by BHP, believes it can solve the problems in the next few months and hit 80,000 tonnes for fiscal 1998, which starts June 1, they said.

Foster's 40 percent owned Molson Breweries reported a C$16.8 million net loss for the year to April 1, compared with a C$75.8 million net profit the previous year. The C$100 million settlement with Coors Brewing more than offset a C$22 million improvement in net income from operations, Molson said.

Plutonic announced on Tuesday that it had signed a A$350 million syndicated debt facility to refinace existing debt and fund acquisitions. This sparked some speculation Plutonic was shaping for a takeover bid for either Great Central Mines, Eagle Mining or Wiluna Mines.

Rio Tinto Plc/Ltd, which owns 71 percent of Coal and Allied and all of Novacaol Pty Ltd, is to hold briefing on its New South Wales coal operations later on Wednesday. The Australian Financial Review reported on Tuesday that Coal and Allied and Novacoal were considering merging their management.
Morgan and Banks reported early on Wednesday a 46 percent rise in annual profit to A$9.87 million in the year to March 31 and raised its final dividend to 14 cents from 10 cents.
Rebel Sport is due to hold a news conference later on Wednesday to announce major changes to its share register and mangement structure.
